lead.headline: Supreme Court blocks Postal Service mail-ballot rules for midterms
lead.dek: Alito and Thomas dissent; Kavanaugh says election officials lack time to comply before November
body: The Supreme Court on Monday, in an unsigned order, refused to let the U.S. Postal Service enforce new mail-ballot regulations before the November midterm elections, leaving in place a lower-court order that blocked rules stemming from a March executive order by President Donald Trump.

The government "is unlikely to succeed on the merits," the unsigned order said. Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented. Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote separately that the Postal Service arguably had authority to issue the rule but that state and local election officials did not have time to implement it before the elections.

The rule would have required states to submit lists of eligible voters to a Postal Service portal and use approved envelope designs, with noncompliant ballots subject to rejection. U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani blocked it in late August, and a second federal judge in Washington did the same Sunday in a suit brought by the Democratic National Committee.

briefs.headline: EPA finalizes repeal of Biden-era power plant carbon limits
briefs.summary: Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the repeal Monday at a G20 energy meeting in Houston, scrapping 2024 carbon-capture rules for coal and new gas plants. Environmental groups said they will sue.

briefs.headline: Pentagon watchdog puts Iran war cost at $33.4B, flags munitions gaps
briefs.summary: The inspector general's first report on Operation Epic Fury says $22.3 billion in munitions spending caused "strategic inventory shortfalls." Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth disputed it.

briefs.headline: Judge blocks DHS four-year cap on foreign student visas
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge F. Dennis Saylor in Boston on Monday enjoined a Homeland Security rule capping student and exchange visas at four years, calling its security rationale "exceptionally weak."

briefs.headline: Pennsylvania measles cases reach 693 as third death is reviewed
briefs.summary: The state Department of Health reported 693 confirmed cases in 38 counties and 133 hospitalizations as of Monday, up 17 since Friday. A third death, reported by a county coroner, is under review.

briefs.headline: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
briefs.summary: Italian fighters on NATO's Baltic mission destroyed a drone that crossed from Belarus early Tuesday, the first shootdown over Lithuanian territory, Lithuanian officials said. Moscow has not commented.

briefs.headline: Saudi Arabia strikes Yemen after Houthi attacks wound 13
briefs.summary: Houthi missile and drone attacks on three Saudi cities wounded 13 civilians, the Saudi-led coalition said. The Houthis said Saudi warplanes then hit five Yemeni governorates with 54 raids in 24 hours.

briefs.headline: Dangote launches $1.6B IPO for Nigerian refinery
briefs.summary: Aliko Dangote opened a share sale Monday seeking $1.6B from retail investors to expand his 650,000-barrel-a-day refinery, Africa's largest IPO. Shares list in Lagos in November.

briefs.headline: Venezuela joins G20 energy talks in Houston at US invitation
briefs.summary: Oil Minister Paula Henao leads a delegation to the Houston meetings running through Wednesday, weeks after Washington finalized a deal for majority control of Venezuela's proven oil reserves.

briefs.headline: Huntington council passes Flock camera guardrails 7-2
briefs.summary: The ordinance approved Monday night caps Flock data retention at seven days and adds a duty to report misuse; the $2.1M contract is still unsigned.

briefs.headline: Morrisey seeks federal disaster aid for three counties
briefs.summary: The governor asked Sunday for individual assistance for Fayette, Harrison and Kanawha after mid-August floods damaged over 600 homes, 22 destroyed.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers float a Raylee's Law compromise at interims
briefs.summary: The bill aired Monday would make principals alert CPS when a child with a substantiated abuse report leaves school; homeschool groups and CPS balked.

briefs.headline: Teaching scholarship has 42 graduates in WV classrooms
briefs.summary: The HEPC chancellor told the Joint Education Committee Monday that 82% of two Underwood Smith cohorts teach high-needs subjects in West Virginia.

regional.item: The mayor told council Monday night a deal is done to build a Kroger Marketplace at 5th Avenue and 24th Street, with equipment already on site.
WVDOT is closing I-64's outside lanes on the Fort Hill Bridge and the Oakwood Road and Virginia Street ramps overnight this week, 8 p.m. to 6 a.m.
Wood County landed five $75,000 site-readiness grants and PowerFlo plans 120 jobs at the old Hino plant in Williamstown, commissioners heard Monday.

away.item: Lake Paran's 13th stone-skipping festival runs Saturday, Sept. 19, 1 to 7 p.m., free to watch and $5 to compete, the Banner reported Sept. 12.

hotspots.item: The 80-foot Red Oak Fire Tower on Bishop Knob, between Cowen and Richwood in the Monongahela National Forest, has opened for overnight stays, the Echo reported Monday.
Surf City holds a public focus group Monday, Sept. 28, 6 to 8 p.m. at the municipal complex in Hampstead on e-bike and multi-use path rules ahead of a December state law.

briefs.headline: RCMP probe death of 77-year-old man in Fort St. James
briefs.summary: Officers called to a disturbance on BC Spruce Road at 2:40 a.m. Monday found him with serious injuries; he died in hospital. The Major Crime Unit said the case appears targeted.

briefs.headline: Osisko approves full build of Cariboo gold mine near Wells
briefs.summary: The 30-month build targets a first gold pour in early 2029; the company said the underground mine will support 613 jobs at peak construction and 525 permanent jobs.

briefs.headline: B.C. deficit forecast climbs $450M to $13.8B
briefs.summary: Finance Minister Josie Osborne's first quarterly update Monday put wildfire spending $614 million over budget; natural gas royalties fell short after a forecasting error.

briefs.headline: Seventh MLA joins Milobar's unnamed B.C. party
briefs.summary: Boundary-Similkameen's Donegal Wilson is the latest of nine Conservative defectors to sign on; the group plans to sit as a caucus when the legislature resumes in October.

briefs.headline: New U.S. 50% tariffs hit 110 Canadian goods
briefs.summary: Levies on furniture, ATVs, motorboats, aluminum and wood products took effect after midnight Tuesday; Washington lifted tariffs on 10 items including salt, cement and toilet paper.

briefs.headline: Alberta NDP takes Calgary-Shaw byelection by 582 votes
briefs.summary: Unofficial results show Kyle Campbell with 7,461 of 16,002 votes over the UCP's Mike Derry, the party's first win there since 2015. Official results are due Sept. 24.

briefs.headline: Vega-C lofts FLEX and Sentinel-3C from French Guiana
briefs.summary: Flight VV30 lifted off at 9:21 p.m. EDT Monday; Sentinel-3C separated about an hour later, FLEX an hour after that, and ESA acquired signals from both.

briefs.headline: ATLAS finds entanglement between Z boson pairs at LHC
briefs.summary: An international team reported in Physical Review Letters strong evidence that pairs of Z bosons from Higgs decays at CERN's ATLAS detector are entangled.

briefs.headline: Single brain implant decodes speech and gestures together
briefs.summary: UCSF researchers reported in Nature Neuroscience that a 253-electrode array in two paralyzed men let an AI decoder produce text and avatar gestures within seconds.

briefs.headline: Perovskite cell makes power 10 meters under the sea
briefs.summary: A Yunnan University team reported in Joule a cell tuned to deep-water light that converted about 35% of it and kept 99.6% of its output after 40 days in seawater.

briefs.headline: UK rights committee calls for AI law and single regulator
briefs.summary: The Joint Committee on Human Rights said Monday that Britain's AI rules are patchy and urged a risk-tiered AI bill, a statutory regulator and mandatory transparency.

briefs.headline: Trump calls AI slowdown push a 'hoax' on call with Huang
briefs.summary: On speaker at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday, Trump told Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang the pause urged by Anthropic's Dario Amodei plays into China's hands.

briefs.headline: Drug firms' private data lifts protein-folding AI
briefs.summary: A consortium including AbbVie and Astex fine-tuned OpenFold3 on 20,167 proprietary structures and predicted over half of 1,056 test cases accurately versus a third before, in a blog post not yet peer-reviewed.

weather_ear: Tuesday's forecast, from Jim Claudtore, lands at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers ran no regional line; the Fed decides Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET, and Liverpool hosts Tottenham in the Carabao Cup at 3 p.m. ET.
